name: Temple Upward Bound and Upward Bound Math & Science
org: Temple University College of Education and Human Development
what_you_do: Free college prep all year. There is tutoring after school on weekdays, Saturday classes, college visits and a six-week summer program on campus. One track focuses on civic work and one on STEM.
who_can_apply: Students in 9th or 10th grade at Philadelphia public district or charter high schools. They come from low-income families, or their parents do not have a bachelor degree, or both. They also plan to go to college. Five named schools get priority. They are Benjamin Franklin HS, Dobbins CTE, Gratz Mastery, Strawberry Mansion and The U School.
pay_detail: Free to students. A pay or stipend is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Runs year-round, with a six-week summer program on campus.
deadline_text: Rolling applications. The page says the Summer Academy deadline is May 31.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send papers that show you are eligible, like a report card, test scores and proof of income. Then you have a virtual interview. Questions: 215-204-3636.
notes: Federally funded and free. You must have a goal of going to college. Income is not the only factor in who is accepted.
